previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted due to a subtherapeutic INR of 1.4 while on chronic warfarin therapy for a mechanical aortic valve. The cause was likely missed doses due to medication confusion. He was started on a heparin drip and resumed his home warfarin regimen. His INR rose to 2.1 within 24 hours and reached 2.4 by discharge, allowing safe discontinuation of heparin. His comorbidities, including diabetes, COPD, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and chronic diastolic heart failure, remained stable throughout the admission. A groin rash was diagnosed as fungal and treated with clotrimazole cream. He was discharged home with instructions to resume all medications, monitor INR the following day, and follow up with his PCP and anticoagulation clinic.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Dyspnea/CP: Patient with known CAD s/p PCI to RCA, in ___ at ___ in ___, who presented 
with sudden dyspnea and chest pain. The patient was at high risk 
for ACS but his EKG revealed no signs of ischemia and he was 
ruled out for MI with 3 sets of negative cardiac biomarkers. 
Records from ___ were obtained and the patient 
had had catheterization in ___, for chest pain, that revealed 
stable disease. We also recieved a TTE report which revealed EF 
of 45-50%. With this new information, his ___ and his 
presenting symptoms a diagnosis of CHF exacerbation was thought 
to be the most likely explanation. He was diuresed with IV 
furosemide and his symptoms improved. Upon discharge he was 
instructed to take furosemide 40 mg daily at home (increased 
from 40 mg every other day). He was continued on his home dose 
medications.  
At the time of discharge (after diuresis), patient was feeling 
well without any complaints of CP or SOB.  He was ambulated, 
including stairs, without recurrance of symptoms.  He was 
scheduled for an outpatient cardiac stress test to further 
ensure that symptoms were not anginal in nature (please see 
below).
.  
# AVR: Patient with mechanical valve aortic valve (likely ___. 
___. On admission his INR was supratherapeutic at 3.7 and his 
coumadin was held. Once INR was therapeutic his coumadin was 
re-started but his dose was reduced to 7.5 mg 4x week and 5 mg 
3x week.  His INR goal range remains 2.5-3.5, due to his 
mechanical valve and other risk factors (hx embolic disease).
.
# DM II: Patient's glyburide was stopped and he was placed on an 
ISS while inpatient. He was instructed to re-start glyburide at 
home on discharge. 
.  
# Eosinophilia: On admission patient was found to have 19% 
eosinophils on CBC with diff. This was calculated to be an 
absolute eosinophilic count of 1,273 representing moderate 
eosinophilia. Upon reviewing past records it was discovered that 
the patient had a history of this. He will need further work up 
as an outpatient. 
.  
# Anemia: Stable and remained at baseline. 
.  
# Back pain: Stable.  
.  
# Code: Patient was full code while inpatient.
